## Figures:

![Fig 1. Example of how local density is estimated. All grey points represent the locations (meters) of censused squirrels on one grid during one spring, with one squirrel randomly selected in red. Density was calculated for each squirrel each spring by tallying the number of censused squirrels whose locations fell within a `r radius` m radius (red circle) of that squirrel's location divided by the area ((pi\*radius\^2)/10000.](Output/Figures/local_density_visual.jpeg)

![Top: Mean local density in control grids across all years of the study. Middle: Local density in response to grid-level treatment. Bottom: Mean local density over time, colored by grid-level treatment.](Output/Figures/density_summary.jpeg)

![Top: litter growth rate (g/day) in response to mother-level treatment, either control, food add with a bucket, food add without a bucket, or rattle playback. Bottom: litter size in response to the same mother-level treatment.](Output/Figures/response_summary.jpeg)

![The relationship between litter growth rate (g/day) and litter size, using control grid data only (n = `r controls[, .N]`).](Output/Figures/GR_littersize.jpeg)

![The relationship between litter growth rate (g/day) and birth date (Julian day), using control grid data only (n = `r controls[, .N]`).](Output/Figures/GR_birthmonth.jpeg)

![Top: litter growth rate (g/day) in response to litter size for control grids only (n = `r controls[, .N]` , colored by local density level. Bottom: litter growth rate (g/day) in response to litter size on food add grids only (n = `r food[, .N]` ), parsed by food add treatment of the mother (with a bucket or without a bucket), and colored by local density level.](Output/Figures/lm_results.jpeg)

![Results from bivariate response models that predict red squirrel litter size and growth rates in response to local density. Upper left: results from control grids only; upper right: results from food add experiments and control grids; lower left: results from control grids during years where cache sizes were measured; lower right: results from rattle playback experiments.](Output/Figures/Bayesian_predictions.jpeg)

![Posterior predictions for each model, control, food add, cache, and rattle](Output/Figures/Posterior_predictions.jpeg)

![Posterior distributions for covariance of litter size and litter growth rate for all three models: control, food add, cache, and rattle.](Output/Figures/Posterior_distributions.jpeg)
